ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the horizontal axis is t, and the vertical axis is f(t). The waveform is a rectangular pulse: from t=0 to t=4, the amplitude is 1; at t=4, it drops to 0; at other positions, it is 0. Reasoning: Therefore it can be written as f(t)=1, 0\le t\le 4, and f(t)=0 for other t. According to the definition of the Fourier transform, \(F(j\omega)=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(t)e^{-j\omega t}\,dt=\int_0^4 e^{-j\omega t}\,dt\). Calculation gives \(F(j\omega)=\left.\frac{e^{-j\omega t}}{-j\omega}\right|_0^4=\frac{1-e^{-j4\omega}}{j\omega}\). Using \(1-e^{-j4\omega}=e^{-j2\omega}(e^{j2\omega}-e^{-j2\omega})=2j e^{-j2\omega}\sin(2\omega)\), therefore \(F(j\omega)=\frac{2\sin(2\omega)}{\omega}e^{-j2\omega}\).
